seo.metaTitle: Unique Color Mask - Find Rare One-Off Pixels
seo.metaDescription: Mark the colors that appear only a few times in an image: compression noise, stray dots and one-off pixels. Free, local, no upload.
seo.longDescription: Most images are built from a small number of repeated colors, so the pixels that appear only once are the odd ones out - a compression artifact, a stray dot, a hot pixel, or a line that was left behind in a photo-editing tool. This tool counts how often each color occurs and marks the ones that do not repeat more than the number you set, as a mask. Raising the rarity limit marks more pixels, which is how you look for artifacts that repeat a few times rather than once. The counting happens in your browser, so the image is never uploaded.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Choose the view: a black and white mask, or a highlight over the original picture.
Set the rarity limit: 1 marks colors that occur once, higher values catch rare colors that repeat a few times.
Set the highlight color and opacity, then download the mask.

faq.q: What counts as a unique color?
faq.a: A color that appears no more often than the rarity limit you set. With the limit at 1 the tool marks the colors that occur exactly once, which in a compressed image are usually artifacts.

faq.q: Why does a photo show a lot of marked pixels?
faq.a: Photographs contain thousands of slightly different shades, and in a large picture many of them occur only a few times. That is expected for photos, and the tool is most useful on flat graphics, logos and icons.

faq.q: What can I do with the mask?
faq.a: Use it to find the pixels that break an otherwise clean image, then remove them with the despeckle tool from this site, or repaint them with the color extract tool.
